releases.name: Tacks 0.2.1: hit locations
releases.notes:
Hit locations: where a hit lands now matters. A preview of `release-0.2.1`, before it merges to `main` (PR #109).

## What's in it

- **Hit Zones.** Every body has six: Head, Torso, Left and Right Arm, Left and Right Leg. They follow the robot's skeleton as it moves. A Head hit costs 1.5× the Tool's damage, a Torso hit 1×, an Arm 0.3× and a Leg 0.5×.
- **Limb Health.** Arms and Legs also wear down on their own. An Arm at 0% drops its Tool as a Dropped Tool, its Hand can hold nothing, and the arm hangs limp for everyone to see. Legs slow you by their average Limb Health: one Leg at 0% is half speed, and with both at 0% you can't walk or jump until you're Ejected or the Round ends. A hurt Leg limps; below 50% it starts to drag on a straight knee, fully at 40%. Limb Health is restored on Respawn and at Round start.
- **Two Hands.** You carry a Tool in each Hand, and **Q** swaps between them in about a quarter of a second, with a hand-change animation. In your own view you see only the active Hand's arm, on its own side. Everyone else sees both Tools, the inactive one lowered.
- **A real Paint Sprayer splash.** It's now a 2 m cone, thickest in the middle, instead of a 4 m ray. It hits everyone inside it, is blocked by shelves and walls, and respects friendly fire. It leaves a Paint Mark on every Hit Zone it touches.
- **Blind per eye.** Paint from the front covers both eyes, from the side one eye, and from behind neither. One painted eye covers that half of your screen. You're fully Blinded only with both eyes covered, and you can still turn, use Tools and swap Hands. Paint on the face shows which eyes are covered and fades with them.
- **Smarter bots.** A Sprayer-armed bot aims at the head and anything else at body centre. Bots see per-eye Blind, swap off a disabled Arm, and with both Arms gone head for a Shelf or Dropped Tool they can reach.
- **Playtest fixes.** The floor no longer flickers on Intel Macs, and shelving casts baked shadows there. Bodies and shots pass through Dropped Tools, and a Blinded player can still turn with the mouse.

## Gameplay

`tacks-0.2.1-ffa-gameplay.mp4` below: Free-for-all against five bots.

## Run it

Open the project in Godot 4.7 and press Play. The game opens on the start menu.

## Known rough edges

- Limb Health never recovers during play (that comes in a later release), so a player with both Legs at 0% waits for Ejection or the Round end.
- On Intel Macs (macOS with Vulkan), players, robots and walls cast no shadows; only the shelving has baked ones.
- A dragged leg swings out and can clip shelving in narrow aisles.

Spec #41, tickets #42–#69 and playtest fixes #99–#106. Full diff: PR #109.

releases.name: Tacks 0.2.0: art pass (latest)
releases.notes:
The v2 art pass: the same rules as 0.1.0, now in a DIY store overrun by two robot factions. A preview of `release-0.2.0`, before it merges to `main` (PR #40).

## What's in it

- **A start menu.** Pick Mode and Difficulty, press Start, and get back to the menu when the Match ends. A Credits screen lists every third-party asset.
- **Two robot factions.** Staff players are a bronze, horned mech and Customers a grey armoured robot. In Free-for-all everyone is a Customer robot. Their glowing lights and eyes show the Team colour (orange or purple), or a different colour for each player in Free-for-all. They idle, run, swing, shoot, flinch when Blinded and fall when Ejected (animations from Quaternius' Universal Animation Library).
- **True first person.** You see your own robot's right arm holding the active Tool, or an open hand when that Hand is empty. Everyone else sees your whole robot.
- **Tool models everywhere.** There's a Kenney Hammer, plus a Nail Gun and a Paint Sprayer made for Tacks in Blender. Each one shows in hand, on its Shelf and on the floor. A Dropped Tool turns slowly with an outline in the Tool's colour.
- **A store that looks like a store.** Kenney shelving and textured floors and walls replace the greybox. Each Shelf shows one Tool per unit of stock, so a bare Shelf looks bare from across the aisle and a Restock visibly refills it.
- **Effects.** Nail tracers, paint mist and hit puffs, and a paint splat over your screen while you're Blinded.

## Gameplay

`tacks-0.2.0-ffa-gameplay.mp4` below: about two minutes of Free-for-all on Easy against five bots, recorded in-engine.

## Run it

Open the project in Godot 4.6 and press Play. The game opens on the start menu.

## Known rough edges

- The robots are lit very dark under the store lighting.
- The robots' joints are rigid, so a small gap can open in the armour when a limb moves.
- In first person, swings play at half strength, and your hidden body still casts a shadow. Other players see your right arm raised and following your aim.
- The held Hammer looks large up close, and in idle its head grazes the robot's thigh.
- Tracers and paint mist start beside the head, not at the held Tool's muzzle. A cleanup ticket from the PR #40 review will fix this.

Tickets #21–#30 of spec #20. Full diff: PR #40.

releases.name: Tacks 0.1.0: bots
releases.notes:
The v1 bot-only prototype: every non-human slot is filled with a bot that plays by the same rules as you.

## What's in it

- **Free-for-all and Team Deathmatch**, chosen with the Mode export on the main scene. In Team Deathmatch you play on Staff with two bot teammates against three Customers.
- **Bots scavenge like you do.** They spawn empty-handed, head for a Shelf drawn by weight (Nail Gun 3, Paint Sprayer 2, Hammer 1), fall back to a nearby Dropped Tool or the next Shelf when one is bare, and pick up opportunistically with a free Hand.
- **Bots fight on line of sight.** Armed bots roam, engage the nearest enemy they can see, use their Tool within its range, and drop the fight the moment you break sight. An empty Nail Gun or Paint Sprayer keeps swinging as weak melee.
- **Easy, Normal and Hard** change only aim and reaction: 12°/0.8 s, 6°/0.45 s, 2°/0.2 s.
- **Blinded bots** hit by your Paint Sprayer fire wildly at where they last saw you for two seconds, with double the aim error.
- **Team colours and Tool markers** on bot bodies, alive counts per Team on the HUD, and Rounds that start on their own after a 3 s pause.
- **A use cooldown per Hand** for everyone: Hammer 0.6 s, Nail Gun 0.15 s, Paint Sprayer 0.5 s, empty melee 0.8 s.

## Gameplay

`tacks-0.1.0-ffa-gameplay.mp4` below: two minutes of Free-for-all on Normal against five bots, recorded in-engine.

## Run it

Open the project in Godot 4.6 and run the main scene. Change Mode and Difficulty on the Main node in the inspector.

## Known playtest risks

- Bots can gather at spawn points, because roam points include them.
- The store has no Departments yet; roam points stand in with the Team Spawn Zone centres.

Tickets #2–#9 of spec #1. Full diff: PR #18.
